newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mergers and acquisitions soar in Brazil - report.
newsitem.headline: Mergers and acquisitions soar in Brazil - report.

text.p: There were at least 259 mergers and acquisitions in Brazil during the first eight months of the year, 42 percent more than in the same period in 1995, according to a report by Price Waterhouse.
The report, published by Gazeta Mercantil, said the value of the mergers and acquisitions totalled $70 million.
Some 157 of the total involved takeovers and acquisitions of minority shareholdings. Another 82 involved joint ventures and the rest involved other transactions, the report said.
The Price Waterhouse count was made from a survey of six Brazilian newspapers in Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
Raul Beer, a partner at Price Waterhouse, told Gazeta that the accounting firm's tally was not comprehensive because many mergers and acquisitions go unreported.
Most of the mergers and acquisitions, especially those involving foreign capital, took place in the food, automobile and consumer goods sectors, the report said.
